assumptions: The refusal doctrine (unhandled constraint -> unresolved with a reason) is the one stated in json-schema.ts's REFUSALS comment and the #1014 issue body, cited there as spec D7 of #765.
An integer range is refused only when both bounds are declared and no integer lies between them; a single fractional bound still has a valid integer default.
A schema declaring both anyOf and oneOf is refused outright rather than intersecting the two.
An explicit undefined override is treated as absent (keeps the default), matching how the unresolved-field guards already treat undefined as missing.

PARKED: union leaf cases still come from members[0] only. Choosing which cases a union should emit (drop cases valid for another member, or per-member cases) is a design decision not covered by D7, so it is left for a follow-up and the keyword is Refs.
